This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 12-08-2021 at about 4.00 a.m. when the petitioner was driving Eicher vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AE-7398 towards Gudivada from Bhimavaram slowly cautious by following all traffic rules, at that time, one Lorry bearing Reg. No.AP- 27-W-6063 parked on the middle of the road near Kanukollu village, Mandavalli Mandal, Krishna District, Andra Pradesh, without taking any precautionary measures, sign boards and indicators, due to beams emerging from opposite coming vehicles on a single road, could not able to locate and anticipate the vehicle parked on the middle of the road, dashed the vehicle to the stationary Lorry, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Govt.
Hospital, Gudivada for first aid treatment and then the doctor referred to Srikala Hospital, Vijayawada and after one day treatment, he was shifted to Sri.Venkateshwara Orthopaedic and Maternity Surgical Specialty Hospital, Mulbagal and spent Rs.3 lakhs to medicines, treatment, conveyance and requires more amount for his future treatment.

entities.text: Venkateshwara Orthopaedic and Maternity Surgical Specialty Hospital, Mulbagal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and earning Rs.20000/-p.m. by working as driver and due to accidental injuries, till today he is bedridden and lost his earnings and in future he cannot do any avocation to earn his livelihood due to disability and impediment.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 remained exparte and respondent No.2 appeared before the Tribunal and filed its Objection Statement.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed in limine and this respondents seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act 1988.

As per Section 134(c) of the MV Act 1988, it is mandatory duty of the respondent No.1 to furnish the particulars of policy, date, time, place of accident, particulars of the injured has not complied with the statutory demand.

As per Section 158(6) of the MV Act 1988, it is mandatory duty of the concerned police station to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of the information, but Jurisdictional Police Authority have failed to forward the documents and not complied with the statutory demand.
Further submitted that, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-27-W-6063 was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

The respondent No.1 by knowingly well willfully used in public place Venu G.S vs Anisetti Venkata Naga Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174564772/
2 and has contravened the proviso of MV Act and rules framed under and have committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: The accident took place due to negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who was driving his Lorry without holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, but not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-27-W-6063.

Further, the compensation amount of petitioner is highly excessive,
exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

4. From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-27-W-6063 on 12.08.2021 at about 4-00 a.m. at Kanukollu village, Mandavalli mandal, Krishna District, Andhra Pradesh?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined one witness PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P18 documents.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
The conflict is only with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioner plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing reg.No.AP-27-W-6063.
Whereas the respondent No.2 contending that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the petitioner and there is a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked 16 documents i.e., FIR, complaint, alteration memo, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, discharge summary, medical prescriptions, accident register,
medical bills, adhar card.

On perusal of the documents, it reveals that soon after the accident,
petitioner filed the complaint before the jurisdictional police and thereafter conducted thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP- 27-W-6063 Anisetti Venkata Naga Kumar for the offence punishable u/s 304A, 338 of IPC by holding that on 12-8-2021 when the petitioner driving his Eicher van bearing No.KA-03-AE-7398 in the early hours proceeding towards Gudivada along with Venkata Naga Kumar and deceased Eri Venkateswara rao hit to the lorry bearing No.AP-27- W-6063 which was negligently parked on the road without taking precautionary steps as petitioner failed to judge the gap and attempted to overtake the lorry
, the offending lorry dashed to the stationed lorry from behind as a result of which petitioner and Venkateswara and the deceased got stuck in the cabin and sustained grievous injuries.

It was held that accused driver of the lorry bearing No.AP-27-W-6063 alleged to have committed an offence punishable u/s 304A, 338 IPC by negligently parked his lorry on the road in the night hours without taking any precautionary steps and thereby caused the accident.

Though respondent counsel denied the contention fo the petitioner and contended that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself but has not examined the driver of the offending lorry or any of the eye witness who are material witness so as to state how the accident had been taken place and tried to disprove the evidence of the petitioner.

Even it is not the case of the respondent that the offending vehicle was not at all parked in the road or else produced any document or adduced evidence to show that he has pllaced indicators and the signals so as to give caution to the vehicles moving on the road.
Only suggestion was made with regard to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner which was out rightly denied by the petitioner.
Apart from this, on perusal of the Ex-P4 sketch, it clearly shows that spot of accident is NH 165 and accident had been taken place on the left side of the road proceeding towards Mandavalli.
Ex-P4 spot mahazar reveals no indicators or signals were placed to safeguard interest of traffic moving on road.

10. The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that lorry was parked on the road without keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road and apart from this, it was dark night.

Precautions prescribed under Section 122 of MV Act read with the relevant Rules have to be followed by the driver and owner of the stationed vehicle,
particularly on a highway.

A duty is cast on the driver as well as the owner of such a vehicle to ensure that such a vehicle is towed away as immediately as practicable and not left abandoned or unattended, particularly on a highway where vehicles are permitted to move at a faster place than on other roads.

In the alternative, some other form of external lighting ought to have been provided so as to give an indication about the parked lorry, until a vehicle, which is stationed/parked due to a break down or if it has met with an accident is towed away, it is necessary that the said vehicle does not become dangerous to other vehicles.

11. Further, in the case of Shashikala Swain & others vs. Md. Khairuddin & another, [AIR 2000 Orissa 52: 2001 ACJ 1638], reference has been made to Section 122 of the Act and the duty cast on the driver of a stationary vehicle on a public place so as not to cause any danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to the users of public place and also to the other passengers.

sentences.text: Further in the judgment of the Gujarat High Court in Premlata Nilamchand Sharma vs. Hirabhai Ranchhodbhai Patel, [1983 ACJ 290] and the judgment of the Delhi High Court in Pushpa Rani Chopra vs. Anokha Singh, [1975 ACJ 396], Hon'ble Apex Court held that where the place was dark and the vehicle was parked without any sign or indication to warn other road users, negligence is on the driver of the parked vehicle and not the driver of any vehicle which dashes into such parked vehicle.

sentences.text: 13. In view of the ratio held in the above decision in the present case, admittedly lorry bearing No.AP- 27-W-6063 was parked on the road without any sign or indication to warn other road users.
Moreover it was dark at 4.00 a.m. early morning.

Under such circumstances, certainly, it can be held that accident had been caused wholly due to the negligence on the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP- 27-W-6063 who had parked the lorry on the road without any indicator and barricade.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused wholly due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP-27-W-6063.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 20 years.
From the Ex-P16-Adhar card it reveals that petitioner's date of birth is 23-4-2002.
Hence as on the date of accident i.e.,2021, petitioner was aged about 19 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was driver and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
15. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-

As per the medical records i.e., Ex- P7-wound certificate reveals that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e.,(1)midshaft  femur displaced fracture (2) proximal 1/3rd tibia/fibula fracture  (3) CLW 2 x 2 cms proximal 1/3rd lateral aspect of right leg and the doctor has opined that the injuries No.1 and 2 are grievous and injuries No.3 is simple in nature.

Ex-P9-discharge summary of Venkateshwara orthopaedics and maternity surgical speciality hospital reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e.,midshaft (R ) femur displaced fracture (2) proximal 1/3rd tibia fracture (Right)/fibula fracture for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 13-8-2021 to 28-8-2021 i.e., for 16 days.

sentences.text: 16. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.2 who stated that, petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., closed fracture displaced midshaft right femur (2) open type II displaced communited fracture proximal 1/rd tibia and fibula right leg and treated by closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing of right femur, MIPPO plating of right proximal tibia under SA on 19-8-2021.
PW-2 further stated that petitioner complains of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged, inability to drive truck

and on examination petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting of right thigh and diffuse Venu G.S vs Anisetti Venkata Naga Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174564772/

PW-2 further stated that recent x-ray shows untied fracture femur with implants in situ, united fracture of proximal tibia and fibula with implants in situ.

So he assessed the disability of right lower limb at 52% and for wholebody at 26%.
17. During cross examination of PW-2

admitted that-            .
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases,
the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.
18.

Considering the nature of injuries, age of petitioner, occupation of petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner being driver can do work with some disability.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 17%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 17%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 20 to 25 is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.5,50,800/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 18 X 17/100) is awarded under this head.
19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., Ex-P7-wound certificate reveals that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e.,(1)midshaft  femur displaced fracture (2)
proximal 1/3rd tibia/fibula fracture  (3) CLW 2 x 2 cms proximal 1/3rd lateral aspect of right leg and the doctor has opined that the injuries No.1 and 2 are grievous and injuries No.3 is simple in nature.

Ex-P9-discharge summary of Venkateshwara orthopaedics and maternity surgical speciality hospital reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e.,midshaft (R ) femur displaced fracture (2) proximal 1/3rd tibia fracture (Right)/fibula fracture for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 13-8-2021 to 28-8- 2021 i.e., for 16 days.

sentences.text: The petitioner has stated that he is suffering from disability and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 19 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 16 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 to 6 months.

sentences.text: Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.90,000/- (15,000 X 6) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
21. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Malur town, Kolar district and has taken treatment at Sri.Venkateshgwara Orthopaedic and maternity surgical speciality hospital, Mulbagal as inpatient for 16 days and underwent surgery and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.
22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

sentences.text: Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.35,000/- is awarded under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical prescriptions at Ex-P10 to 13.
Medical bills at Ex-P15 for Rs.1,35,392/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident,
the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.1,35,392/- under the head of medical expenses.
24. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The doctor has stated that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants at both sites would cost around Rs.50,000/- in a private setup.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his future medical expenses.
However, by considering the say of doctor, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, awarding of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses would be justified.

Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.9,71,192/-.
26. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
27. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,71,192/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that lorry was parked on the road without keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road and apart from this, it was dark night.
Precautions prescribed under Section 122 of MV Act read with the relevant Rules have to be followed by the driver and owner of the stationed vehicle,
particularly on a highway.
A duty is cast on the driver as well as the owner of such a vehicle to ensure that such a vehicle is towed away as immediately as practicable and not left abandoned or unattended, particularly on a highway where vehicles are permitted to move at a faster place than on other roads.
In the alternative, some other form of external lighting ought to have been provided so as to give an indication about the parked lorry, until a vehicle, which is stationed/parked due to a break down or if it has met with an accident is towed away, it is necessary that the said vehicle does not become dangerous to other vehicles.
Venu G.S vs Anisetti Venkata Naga Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174564772/
4 12.
Further in the judgment of the Gujarat High Court in Premlata Nilamchand Sharma vs. Hirabhai Ranchhodbhai Patel, [1983 ACJ 290] and the judgment of the Delhi High Court in Pushpa Rani Chopra vs. Anokha Singh, [1975 ACJ 396], Hon'ble Apex Court held that where the place was dark and the vehicle was parked without any sign or indication to warn other road users, negligence is on the driver of the parked vehicle and not the driver of any vehicle which dashes into such parked vehicle.
Under such circumstances, certainly, it can be held that accident had been caused wholly due to the negligence on the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP- 27-W-6063 who had parked the lorry on the road without any indicator and barricade.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,71,192/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
